note.backdrop: The morning's mild bounce has gone. At 12:37 ET the S&P 500 fund was -0.4%, the Nasdaq 100 fund -0.1%, small companies +0.6% and the VIX -0.8%. GuruFocus (on Yahoo) has the Dow down 420 points, with health insurers, energy and industrials doing the damage and Nvidia reversing its gains. The day split by industry, not by market: health insurers about -6%, refiners about -5%, gold miners about -4%, while clothing and discount retailers rose 4-11% and security software 5-14%. Oil fell 5.2% by the check's measure and gold 2.9%. 60 stocks are outside their 2-in-3 range and 7 outside their 9-in-10 range, from 10 and 3 this morning. The four flags that rested on single early prints all settled: Northwest Natural +0.3%, HEICO +1.0%, Neogen -0.1%, Welltower +0.5%.

read.says: Dow -420 points (-0.8%), S&P 500 -0.1%, Nasdaq +0.5% at mid-morning; Nvidia reversed earlier gains to trade under 1% lower despite beating and lifting its fiscal 2028 growth forecast to 75%; healthcare, energy and industrials weighed; Anthropic could price above its $70-$78 range.

UnitedHealth fell 5.42% to $389.68 on Nov 17 after CMS's Nov 16 CRUSH proposal: Medicare Advantage audits extrapolated from samples back to payment year 2018, the fee-for-service adjuster dropped, about $9 billion a payment year recovered industrywide; comments due Jan 19, 2027; a 2023 rule with the same features was vacated in Sept 2025 and is on appeal at the Fifth Circuit; UnitedHealth has not quantified its exposure.

UnitedHealth fell 5.4% on Nov 17 with no company announcement; all seven other managed-care companies worth $2 billion or more fell (median -3.9%); its net margin over the twelve months to September was 3.5%.

Cybersecurity stocks rose after the Homeland Security Secretary's House testimony on AI-powered cyberattacks on US infrastructure, including Iranian activity since February: Palo Alto +6% (it reports after today's close; consensus EPS $0.97 on $3.31 billion), CrowdStrike +6%, Fortinet and Check Point +5%, Zscaler +4.8%, SentinelOne +9%, Rubrik +7.5%; ServiceNow and Workday -3.5%, Salesforce -3.7%.

EIA: US crude stocks +3.4 million barrels (poll +58,000), gasoline +5.2 million (poll +1.6 million), distillates +1.6 million; Brent -1.2% to $92.02 and WTI -1.9% to $84.38 at 10:46 ET, WTI at its lowest since late August; the US-Iran conflict (Iran struck US sites in Kuwait after a US strike on Qeshm Island) curbed the fall; both benchmarks on track for about -20% this month on rising Middle East exports.

Newmont -5.13% to $105.56 at 9:40 ET as December gold fell to about $3,767.60, tied by Yahoo Finance to a 96.7% FedWatch probability of a Fed rate increase; at that price its margin over a $1,520 cost guide is about $2,248 an ounce, about 20% less than at its third-quarter realized price of $4,317.

TJX third quarter: comparable sales +4% (above plan), Marmaxx +2%; sales $16.0 billion (+6%); EPS $1.39, adjusted $1.34 (+5%) excluding a $0.05 net tariff-refund benefit; adjusted gross margin -0.5 point on freight and fuel; the chief executive expects sales momentum to accelerate through the holidays.
Cal-Maine: avian influenza at a Florida facility; about 1.4 million laying hens and 360,000 pullets, 2.7% of its flock, will be depopulated; production there has stopped.
Before the open: markets priced a 96.8% probability of a 25-basis-point Fed rate increase in December; gold down more than 2% below $3,800; oil about -2%.
Target's third quarter: sales $27.1 billion (+7.1%), comparable sales +5.6% against a 3.61% estimate, diluted EPS $2.65 including a $0.50 tariff-refund benefit.

singles.beneath: The stock has sat at the offering price all day. Its hospital partners fell too (HCA -3.3%, Tenet -2.3%) on the insurers' news, which makes it hard to tell how much of the last bit is the offering.
singles.cause: Ardent Health is -19.9%, at $14.38, just under the $14.50 its holders sold 8 million shares at last night (its pricing release).

singles.beneath: The guide is about flat once fiscal 2026's $37 million of inventory charges are set aside. A stock 67% below its high rising 23% on a flat year says the price had assumed worse; my reading, unchanged from the morning.
singles.cause: BellRing is +23.1%, from +14.4% before the open, after results and a fiscal 2027 outlook of sales from a 3% decline to 1% growth (its release; MarketBeat on its call).

singles.beneath: The fall deepened as the session confirmed it, unlike Ecovyst's, which eased from -10.0% to -6.6%. Its payments-software partners are flat. About $490 million of value on a $6.0 billion company.
singles.cause: ACI Worldwide is -8.2%, from -4.4% before the open: its chief executive is leaving and insiders lead until a replacement is found (its 8-K; Payments Dive's summary).

singles.beneath: Half the morning's fall came back once trading began: the reaffirmed guidance carried more weight in session than before it.
singles.cause: Ecovyst is -6.6%, from -10.0% before the open, after its chief executive's departure and reaffirmed guidance (its 8-K; Investing.com).

singles.beneath: A beat on lowered numbers with margins improving; the stock moves with McCormick and Flowers (+3.3% each today), so part of it is food stocks rising with the defensive rotation, my inference.
singles.cause: J&J Snack Foods is +7.7%: its quarter beat forecasts with a better gross margin, though adjusted earnings were lower and sales fell 1% (InvestorsHub; MarketBeat on its call).

singles.beneath: The largest US egg producer rose on losing birds: my inference is that the market reads a first outbreak of the migration season as the start of wider culls that cut national egg supply and raise prices, which pays the biggest producer more than the 2.7% of its flock it loses.
singles.cause: Cal-Maine is +8.6% after reporting avian influenza at a Florida facility: about 1.4 million laying hens and 360,000 pullets, 2.7% of its flock, will be culled (its release).

themes.beneath: In proportion: UnitedHealth was worth $351.5 billion at Tuesday's close, so today's 8.1% is about $28 billion, on top of Tuesday's 5.2%; Humana's 8.9% is about $4.8 billion. Together that is already several years of the industry's estimated $9 billion a year, for two companies alone; my inference is that the market is pricing lower margins ahead, not only repayments. UnitedHealth's net margin was 3.5% over the last year, so there is little room to absorb a cost like this. The rule is not final: comments close Jan 19, 2027, and an earlier rule with the same features was struck down in 2025 and is on appeal.
themes.cause: The CRUSH proposal of Nov 16 would extrapolate Medicare Advantage audit findings back to payment year 2018 without the fee-for-service adjuster; CMS estimates about $9 billion a payment year recovered across the industry (TradingKey; Trefis). On Tuesday the group's median fell 3.9%. Today it is down a further 6.1%: UnitedHealth -8.1%, Humana -8.9%, Centene -6.1%, Elevance -6.0%, Molina -5.6%, Oscar -4.9%, Cigna -3.0%, CVS -3.2%; the Medicare Advantage care groups agilon -15.5%, Alignment -8.8%, Clover -7.4%. I found no new report today; today's leg is unexplained by a source.
themes.mechanism: The rule turns revenue already booked for 2018 onward into a possible repayment, and cuts what future coding earns. The fall lines up with exposure: the companies most tied to Medicare Advantage (Humana, UnitedHealth, agilon, Alignment, Clover) fell most, those with more commercial or pharmacy business (Cigna, CVS) least. That ranking is my reading of the moves, not a source's.
themes.name: Health insurers fell a second day, harder than the first

read_through.why: hospitals are paid by these insurers; tighter Medicare Advantage money could slow payments to providers (untested; HCA -3.3% today, its partner)

themes.watch: Any insurer sizing its exposure or reserving for 2018-2024; the Fifth Circuit's decision on the 2023 rule; whether the group steadies tomorrow without news.

themes.beneath: The same morning, the application software that sold off on Tuesday kept falling: Salesforce -3.3%, HubSpot -4.5%, Adobe -3.4%, Atlassian -3.2%, ServiceNow -2.3%. My inference: investors are splitting software into what AI threatens (seats in business applications, a day before Anthropic trades) and what AI makes more needed (security). The cluster is tied by a year of moving together, not by any company news.
themes.cause: Cybersecurity stocks rose after the Homeland Security Secretary told a House committee about AI-powered attacks on US infrastructure, including Iranian activity since February (Seeking Alpha on TradingView). Fastly +14.4%, Tenable +13.4%, Rapid7 +10.4%, Okta +9.1%, Qualys +9.0%, SentinelOne +7.9%, Rubrik +7.7%, Palo Alto +7.6%, Zscaler +6.5%, Cloudflare +6.5%, CrowdStrike +5.3%, Fortinet +5.3%, A10 +8.0%. Palo Alto reports after today's close.
themes.mechanism: Testimony changes no budget today; it reminds buyers that security spending is the part of IT that grows when threats rise, and the stocks that move together all year (Tenable with Qualys 0.79, Okta with CrowdStrike 0.77) moved together today. Palo Alto's report tonight is the first real number on demand. That the testimony is the trigger rather than positioning ahead of Palo Alto is the source's account; I cannot separate the two.
themes.name: Security software up on the Homeland Security testimony; application software down again
themes.watch: Palo Alto's results and guidance tonight; whether the group holds the gain tomorrow if they disappoint; whether application software recovers after Anthropic's first trade on Thursday.

themes.beneath: The numbers are modest: TJX's adjusted earnings rose 5%, its core Marmaxx division's comparable sales 2%, and its adjusted margin fell 0.5 point on freight and fuel. What moved the stocks is my inference: relief that holiday demand is holding after a run of weak retail shares, plus Target's comparable sales of +5.6%. This morning I wrote that Target's tariff refund explained its muted reaction; that is wrong, as the stock is up 6.8%. TJX's refund was only $0.05 a share.
themes.cause: TJX reported comparable sales +4% (above plan) and adjusted EPS of $1.34 (+5%), and expects holiday sales momentum to accelerate (its release; Retail Dive; Tikr). TJX +11.1%. Target, -0.5% before the open, is +6.8%. Burlington +6.6%, Ross +4.1%, Macy's +7.5%, Caleres +7.5%, Steve Madden +6.5%, Urban Outfitters +6.3%, Kontoor +7.7%, American Eagle +4.8%, Abercrombie +4.2%, Gap +3.2%.
themes.mechanism: TJX and Target are the first big readings on how shoppers enter the holidays; better than planned sales at the two lifts every chain that sells to the same households. The off-price peers (Burlington, Ross) and the mall apparel and shoe names that move with Macy's moved most.
themes.name: Discount and apparel retail rallied on TJX and Target
themes.watch: Walmart and other big retailers' reports in the coming days; whether the apparel names hold the gain without their own news.

themes.beneath: In proportion: the check reads oil -5.2% from Yahoo's front-month WTI, which rolled today from the December contract ($86.01 at Tuesday's close) to January ($81.73 now, against its own $84.65 close). December alone is about -3.9%, January -3.5%; the roll's December-to-January gap adds about 1 to 1.5 points. This morning I inferred that easing Middle East risk drove both oil and gold; the reports say the opposite: the Middle East fighting escalated overnight and held oil up, and the fall came from US stocks.
themes.cause: The EIA reported US crude stocks up 3.4 million barrels against a poll of 58,000, and gasoline up 5.2 million against 1.6 million; WTI hit its lowest since late August, while the US-Iran fighting (Iran struck US sites in Kuwait after a US strike on Qeshm Island) curbed the fall (Business Recorder). Refiners' median -4.7%: CVR -8.7%, Delek -6.9%, Par -6.6%, PBF -6.2%, HF Sinclair -6.0%, Valero -4.8%, Marathon -4.7%, Phillips 66 -3.4%; producers about -3% (Chevron -4.1%, Occidental -3.7%, ConocoPhillips -2.9%).
themes.mechanism: Refiners earn the gap between fuel and crude. A gasoline build three times what was expected says fuel demand is weak, which narrows that gap even as crude falls, so refiners fell more than producers. That reading is mine.
themes.name: Oil fell on a US stock build, refiners fell most; the check overstates oil's fall
themes.watch: Whether refiners recover if gasoline demand data improves next week; the check's oil line is wrong whenever the front contract rolls (a flaw, like the after-close futures line).

themes.beneath: The reported cause is weak as an explanation of today: the hike probability was already about 97% before the open, and the 10-year yield fell 0.04 point today, which is not what fresh hike bets do. So the cause of gold's fall is not established; neither is this morning's common root with oil, which the oil reports contradict.
themes.cause: Gold -2.9%. Yahoo Finance and GuruFocus tie the slide to a 96.7% probability of a Fed rate increase on CME's FedWatch; Newmont -6.2%, Coeur -6.8%, Hecla -6.4%, SSR Mining -7.7%, Royal Gold -4.2%; the miners' median -3.9%. Barrick is +3.7%, against the group; I did not look into why.
themes.mechanism: A miner's margin is the gold price less its cost: at about $3,768, Newmont's margin over its $1,520 cost guide is about $2,248 an ounce, about 20% less than at its third-quarter realized price of $4,317 (GuruFocus). The stocks that move most with gold moved two to three times what their usual rate implies (Newmont -6.2% against -1.9%).
themes.name: Gold miners fell further as gold dropped below $3,800
themes.watch: The Fed minutes this afternoon; whether gold steadies if yields keep falling.

themes.beneath: In proportion, against the desk's calls from Nov 13's close: Nvidia at $152.13 is 6.6% below $162.89 (the call needs 7.5%, a close at or below $150.67 on Friday); Dell at $314.79 is 8.2% below $342.98 (needs 9.5%, at or below $310.40); AMD at $516.13 is 3.1% below $532.84 (needs 9%). My reading: the report settled whether spending grows but not who pays for it, and money moved to security software and retail today.
themes.cause: Nvidia reversed its gains despite beating and raising its fiscal 2028 growth outlook to 75% (GuruFocus on Yahoo). Nvidia -1.5%, CoreWeave -4.7%, Dell -2.9%, IREN -1.8%, Marvell -1.4%, Sandisk -1.1%; Super Micro +3.2%, Vertiv +3.5% and Broadcom +2.2% held up.
themes.mechanism: This morning's watch said a close back near Tuesday's lows would mean the report changed little; by midday most of the group is below Tuesday's close. The source says investors weighed the results against broader worries about the AI trade.
themes.name: The AI build-out gave back the whole post-report rally
themes.watch: Friday's close against the three call thresholds; Anthropic's price tonight.

threads: Health insurers: did anything new come out today, and does the group steady tomorrow?
Palo Alto reports tonight: does security software keep today's gain?
Anthropic prices tonight and trades Thursday: does application software recover after it?
The desk's size calls are judged Friday against Nov 13's close: Nvidia is 6.6% below (needs 7.5%), Dell 8.2% below (needs 9.5%), AMD 3.1% below (needs 9%).
Retail: do the apparel and off-price names hold their gains?
The Fed's October minutes this afternoon, and gold.
The check's oil line includes today's WTI contract roll (about 1.3 points of the -5.2%): a flaw to fix, like the after-close futures line.
Primo Brands: two sessions outside its range with no cause found.
Barrick +3.7% against falling gold miners: not looked into.
Capricor and Savara FDA decisions by Sunday Nov 22 (both up today, +9.0% and +5.4%); Inhibrx data Nov 19-20.

unexplained.tried: -7.1%, outside its 9-in-10 range, after -6.6% before the open. No filing and no story; web searches found only the Nov 16 refinancing ($700 million of 7.625% notes) and older analyst changes. Its beverage partners rose (Celsius +5.8%), so it is not its industry.
+8.5%, no filing and no story; a beverage company rising while Primo Brands falls.
+13.0%, no filing and no story; one weak partner only.
+6.5%, no filing and no story naming it.
+8.0%; the only story is DoorDash and Lyft's joint rewards program, published at 2:07 ET, before a morning in which Lyft did not flag.
